extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists, and Reddit users seeking an encyclopedic overview of Reddit
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of Reddit covering its history, features, moderation practices, policy changes, and controversies. The page summarizes factual details and public-facing policies rather than providing a prescriptive how-to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subreddit language policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual subreddits may opt to cater to a specific language other than English, and only allowing posts and comments to be in that language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site's display interface is available in several common languages, but most user-submitted content is written in English with no built-in translation feature. Subreddits can set language-specific rules (e.g., allow only posts/comments in a given language) to shape community discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account/registration requirements for participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit can be viewed without an account but registration is required to submit, comment or vote. Registration is also occasionally required to view posts marked as not safe for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viewing is generally open, but contributing (posting, commenting, voting) requires an account; some content (NSFW) may be gated behind registration. This is a platform-level participation rule affecting accessibility and moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics on the platform (consent & impersonation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An experiment was run without the consent or knowledge of the subreddit moderators for four months ... Critics of the experiment argued it was unethical as it involved impersonation and involuntarily used Redditors as experiment participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices that involve studying or influencing Reddit users should consider moderator and user consent and avoid impersonation; lack of consent and covert manipulation are flagged as unethical in coverage of platform research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-harassment policy and subreddit bans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit launched a harassment crackdown and banned subreddits under an anti-harassment policy (e.g., 'These are the 5 subreddits Reddit banned under its game-changing anti-harassment policy — and why it banned them').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and communities that violate harassment rules can be subject to removal or community bans. The page documents both policy adoption and concrete enforcement actions as examples of how Reddit polices abusive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation enforcement practice: shadowbans vs account suspensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit Replaces Its Confusing Shadowban System With Account Suspensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform moved from opaque 'shadowban' behavior to clearer account suspension practices, indicating a principle toward more transparent and explicit enforcement actions rather than hidden penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency reporting and removal statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Transparency', 'Transparency Report 2020', and statements like 'Reddit removed 6% of all posts made last year'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reddit publishes transparency reports and removal metrics to document moderation activity and platform enforcement; these reports are used to communicate scale and types of content actions to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator labor and volunteer moderation norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit moderators do $3.4 million worth of unpaid work each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community moderation is largely performed by unpaid volunteers (subreddit moderators); this fact informs discussions of moderation capacity, reliance on volunteers, and debates over platform responsibility vs community labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with age-verification and legal/regulatory rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit introduces age verification in the UK ahead of new rules and rolled out age verification to comply with new rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform must implement technical and policy measures (e.g., age verification) to comply with jurisdictional regulations protecting minors; the page documents deployment in response to legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official channels to communicate product and policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous references to posts like 'Addressing the community about changes to our API', 'r/announcements', blog posts and archived announcements about login flow and product changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reddit communicates major policy and product changes through official community channels (r/announcements, reddit blog, changelogs); maintaining an archive and clear announcements is treated as the platform's expected practice for community-facing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page/content curation restrictions (explicit content management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit is eliminating explicit content from its public homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform-level curation may remove or limit explicit/NSFW content from public-facing aggregations (e.g., front page/r/all) while leaving community-level content controls in place; this is an example of balancing community content and public presentation.
